name: Potassium chloride
executiveSummary: K⁺ replacement. Pediatrics: maint. **1–3 mEq/kg/day** (<1 y: **2–6**); symptomatic hypokalemia IV **0.5–1 mEq/kg/dose**. Usual rate **≤0.25 mEq/kg/h** (common max **20 mEq/h**). Never undiluted IV.
indications:
## Indications

- Hypokalemia; replacement of losses; maintenance in fluid therapy.

## Precautions

- **Never give concentrate undiluted.** Risk of arrest from iatrogenic hyperkalemia.
- CKD, potassium-sparing diuretics, ACEI/ARB, NSAIDs.
- Correct concomitant hypomagnesemia.

> 1 g KCl ≈ **13.5 mEq** K⁺. Common ampules **3 mEq/mL**.

adulto.presentation: Ampules 10–20 mEq; premix bags; PO ER 8 mEq/cap.
adulto.dose: Typical replacement **10–40 mEq** per diluted dose; oral maint. **40–80 mEq/day** in divided doses (common max **20 mEq**/PO dose).
adulto.infusionRate: Peripheral usual **≤10 mEq/h**; with monitoring/central may be higher per protocol (common max **20 mEq/h**).
adulto.administration: IV **only diluted** (peripheral < **60 mEq/L**; central up to **150–200 mEq/L** orient.).

pediatrico.presentation: Ampules **3 mEq/mL**; PO compounded solution ~3 mEq/mL; ER caps 8 mEq.
pediatrico.dose: Maintenance: **<1 y: 2–6 mEq/kg/day**; **>1 y: 1–3 mEq/kg/day**. Symptomatic hypokalemia IV: **0.5–1 mEq/kg/dose**. Asymptomatic PO: ~**3 mEq/kg/day** + losses.
pediatrico.notes: Usual IV rate **≤0.25 mEq/kg/h**; common max **20 mEq/h**. Compatible NS/D5W.

neonatal.dose: Maintenance **1–2 mEq/kg/day** IV via pump; symptomatic correction **0.5–1 mEq/kg** slow under monitoring.
neonatal.administration: Central IV preferred; never concentrated bolus.

stability:
## Stability

- Use dedicated line when possible; verify final concentration before connecting.
adverseEffects:
## Adverse effects

PO: nausea, abdominal pain. IV: phlebitis, paresthesias, arrhythmias, block, arrest.
